summary: The enterprise AI model API aggregator landscape in 2026 is dominated by the three hyperscalers—AWS Bedrock, Microsoft Azure AI Foundry (formerly Azure AI Studio/OpenAI Service), and Google Vertex AI Model Garden—each offering broad model access within a customer's secure cloud perimeter. Data-platform-native options like Snowflake Cortex AI (over 5,200 weekly active accounts) and Databricks are gaining strong momentum by bringing models to where enterprise data already lives, while IBM watsonx, Oracle Cloud AI, and Cloudflare Workers AI serve specialized governance, existing-relationship, and edge-inference needs. The common thread is secure managed access to foundation models without proprietary data leaving the governed environment.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy: models run within the enterprise's existing cloud/VPC perimeter so sensitive data and prompts never leave the governed environment or get used for vendor training.

Unified compliance and governance: built-in audit logging, access controls, and certifications (SOC 2, HIPAA, FedRAMP, GDPR) satisfy regulatory requirements across one platform instead of vetting each model vendor separately.

Single billing and consolidated contracts: model consumption rolls into existing cloud commitments and enterprise discount agreements (EDPs, committed-use), simplifying procurement and cost management.

Model choice and avoiding lock-in: one API surface provides access to many foundation model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, and native models), allowing teams to switch or multi-source models without re-architecting.

Enterprise integration: native connectivity to existing identity (IAM/Entra), data stores, RAG/vector search, fine-tuning, and agent orchestration reduces integration effort versus stitching together direct vendor APIs.

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token (input/output per 1M tokens) with on-demand, provisioned throughput, and batch rates; model-specific pricing e.g. gpt-oss-120b standard and batch tiers. No markup beyond model cost.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises with primary workloads already on AWS seeking the broadest multi-provider model choice under existing cloud contracts.

platforms.name: Azure AI Foundry (Azure OpenAI Service)
available_models: DeepSeek and other open models via catalog
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per-token plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved capacity; caching discounts and batch pricing available.
key_features: Azure Monitor and diagnostic audit logs
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-centric enterprises wanting privileged access to the latest OpenAI models with deep M365/Entra integration.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token / per-character with on-demand and committed-use discounts; provisioned throughput and batch pricing for supported models.
key_features: Grounding with Google Search / enterprise data
Strong multimodal and data analytics integration
platforms.best_for: Data- and multimodal-heavy enterprises on Google Cloud needing Gemini plus a large third-party model catalog.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
available_models: Reka and other hosted Cortex LLMs
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based, billed in Snowflake credits as part of product revenue; charged per-token for LLM functions with no separate infra to manage.
key_features: Models run inside Snowflake security perimeter
No data movement out of the data cloud
platforms.best_for: Enterprises whose critical data lives in Snowflake wanting AI and natural-language analytics directly on governed data; surpassed 5,200 weekly active accounts in 2026.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs); pay-per-token for Foundation Model APIs plus provisioned throughput options.
key_features: Mosaic AI model serving and fine-tuning
platforms.best_for: Data engineering and ML teams on the lakehouse wanting to fine-tune and serve custom models alongside governed data pipelines.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx
platforms.pricing: Subscription plus consumption (Resource Units) for model inference and tuning; requires commercial scrutiny of contract structure for long-term flexibility.
key_features: watsonx.governance for model risk and compliance
platforms.best_for: Regulated enterprises with existing IBM relationships prioritizing governance, hybrid/on-prem deployment, and AI risk management.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token on-demand and dedicated AI cluster (reserved capacity) pricing; integrated into OCI consumption and Universal Credits.
platforms.best_for: Oracle ERP/database customers and sovereignty-sensitive enterprises wanting generative AI within OCI and dedicated regions.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-use billed in 'Neurons' / per-request on a serverless model; low-latency edge pricing with generous free tier.
key_features: AI Gateway for caching, rate limiting, and logging
Data Localization Suite for residency control
platforms.best_for: Developers and enterprises needing fast, low-latency edge inference for open models and a governance gateway in front of external APIs.
